security_audit.summary: Reviewed 959 static findings. Most were Markdown documentation false positives, including shell backtick detections, example URLs, and SDK reference snippets; confirmed local file writes in helper scripts and third-party Google query submission. No prompt injection or malware intent was found, but the skill has medium contextual risk from anti-detection scraping guidance and optional LLM-based processing of crawled content.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts write crawl outputs to fixed filenames.
remediation.suggestion: Add output path options, warn before overwriting files, and document where markdown, screenshots, and JSON results are stored.

remediation.issue: Anti-detection guidance can enable policy-violating scraping.
remediation.suggestion: Replace evasion-focused wording with guidance to respect robots.txt, site terms, rate limits, and permission boundaries.

remediation.issue: LLM extraction can disclose crawled page content to external providers.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy warning and recommend CSS extraction for private, regulated, or authenticated pages.

remediation.issue: The Google search helper sends user queries to Google.
remediation.suggestion: Document the third-party request, provider policy risk, and alternatives for users who cannot share search terms externally.

content.value_statement: Web pages are hard to turn into clean, reusable data. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused Crawl4AI workflows for crawling, markdown, and extraction.
actual_capabilities: Crawl a single URL with the Crawl4AI CLI or Python SDK.
Convert web pages into clean markdown for review or reuse.
Extract structured data with CSS schemas, XPath patterns, or LLM strategies.
Process multiple URLs concurrently with the provided batch crawler script.
Handle JavaScript-heavy pages with wait conditions, sessions, and browser configuration.
Save markdown, JSON results, and optional page screenshots to local files.
limitations: Requires Crawl4AI and its browser dependencies to be installed locally.
Target websites may block automated crawlers or prohibit scraping in their terms.
LLM extraction can require API keys and may send page content to a provider.
Provided scripts use fixed default output filenames unless edited by the user.

use_cases.title: Turn Documentation Into Markdown
use_cases.description: Crawl product docs or knowledge base pages and produce clean markdown for indexing, review, or summarization.

use_cases.title: Build Repeatable Extraction Schemas
use_cases.description: Generate or refine selectors for product, article, or listing pages, then reuse them without repeated LLM calls.

use_cases.title: Audit Dynamic Page Content
use_cases.description: Load JavaScript-heavy pages, wait for target elements, and inspect links, media, metadata, and extracted content.

prompt_templates.title: Crawl One Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Crawl4AI to crawl this URL and return clean markdown. Tell me which command you will run before running it: <url>

prompt_templates.title: Extract A Page Section
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused extraction from a known page area
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Crawl4AI to extract only the main article content from <url>. Ignore navigation, ads, cookie banners, and unrelated sidebars.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Reusable Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the extraction pipeline to design a reusable CSS schema for <url>. The target fields are title, price, image, and product link.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Batch Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Crawl these URLs as a batch, summarize extraction quality, list failures, and recommend selector or timeout changes: <urls>

output_examples.input: Crawl a documentation page and return markdown.
output_examples.output: A concise report with the page title, crawl status, link counts, and a clean markdown version of the main content.

output_examples.input: Extract product listings from a shop page.
output_examples.output: A structured summary of product names, prices, and links, plus notes about missing fields or selector problems.

output_examples.input: Run a batch crawl across several source pages.
output_examples.output: A batch summary with successful pages, failed pages, content lengths, output file locations, and recommended retries.

best_practices: Confirm permission, robots.txt, and rate limits before crawling a target site.
Prefer CSS or XPath extraction for repeatable public data before using LLM extraction.
Use explicit output directories and review saved files for sensitive content.
anti_patterns: Do not crawl authenticated, private, or regulated pages without a clear data handling plan.
Do not use proxy or user-agent settings to evade a site policy or access controls.
Do not paste real API keys into prompts, YAML files, or shared extraction examples.

faq.question: Does this skill install Crawl4AI automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and scripts, but the user must install Crawl4AI and browser dependencies in the local environment.

faq.question: Can it crawl JavaScript-heavy pages?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents wait conditions, browser settings, sessions, and timeouts for pages that render content with JavaScript.

faq.question: Does it require an LLM provider?
faq.answer: No. CSS, XPath, regex, and markdown workflows can run without LLM calls. LLM extraction is optional.

faq.question: Where are outputs saved?
faq.answer: The helper scripts save local markdown, JSON, schema, and screenshot files in the working directory by default.

faq.question: Is this suitable for private websites?
faq.answer: Use caution. Private or authenticated content may be saved locally or sent to an LLM provider if those options are enabled.

faq.question: Can it scrape Google search results?
faq.answer: The included script targets Google search pages, but users should review provider policies and avoid prohibited automated access.
